# Release Notes Writing Guide

This guide defines how our team drafts, reviews, and publishes release
notes for the Acme Analytics platform.

## Audience and tone

Release notes serve two audiences: administrators planning upgrades and
support engineers triaging incidents. Write in present tense, second
person. Avoid marketing language entirely.

## Versioning scheme

Acme Analytics uses semantic versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. A MAJOR
bump may remove or change existing behavior. A MINOR bump adds
features without breaking changes. A PATCH bump fixes defects only.

Every release must state its version and release date in the first
heading block of the notes.

## Drafting workflow

Start from the merged pull-request list for the milestone. For each
user-facing change, capture what changed, why it matters, and any
action the reader must take. Changes that require no action still
need a plain-language sentence.

Drafts are due three business days before the release date. The
documentation reviewer checks terminology against the glossary and
verifies every command example runs on a staging environment.

## Breaking changes section

Any release that renames, removes, or changes the default value of a
public setting MUST include a migration step. Migration steps follow
this pattern: state the old behavior, state the new behavior, then
give the exact command or setting change required.

If no migration is possible, say so explicitly and describe the
supported workaround and its expiration date.

## Publishing checklist

- Version and date appear in the header
- Every breaking change has a migration step
- Commands were verified on staging
- Terminology matches the current glossary
- Known issues list links to incident tickets

## Rollback guidance

Each minor or major release note must describe how to roll back to
the previous version. Include the rollback command, the expected
downtime, and which data, if any, is affected.

Patch releases do not require rollback guidance unless they touch
database migrations.
